reviews.reason: The bialternant quotient is used only at ranks at least the partition length; the new zero components below that length agree with the inverse-limit identity and do not alter either determinant proof.

The finite Cauchy–Binet expansion uses Schur quotients only for partitions with length at most the chosen rank; zero components at shorter ranks contribute no terms and preserve the stable bidegree identity.
The new below-length zero convention states exactly the rank-N specialization used here; the independent dual Jacobi–Trudi computation s_(1^(N+1))=e_(N+1) gives the same zero, including N=0.
The antipodal map exchanges the two marked endpoints of the digon and therefore satisfies the new corner-preserving pairing premise; the cyclic link and projective-plane quotient are unchanged.

The proof already prescribes marked boundary points under its disk reparametrizations and subdivides paired sides at corresponding image points; all resulting pairings preserve corners, so the stronger schema interface is satisfied.
The square side maps are affine maps between closed intervals and send endpoints to endpoints; their corner classes and single cyclic link therefore remain valid under the repaired schema definition.
Both torus side identifications map endpoints to endpoints and are affine; the four corner sectors still form one cyclic vertex link, so the strengthened schema condition changes no use here.
The cited torus and Klein bottle square pairings both preserve their marked corners; their compact surface, Euler characteristic, and differing orientability conclusions remain licensed.

Its map definition quantifies over genuine covering atlases, exactly as the repaired Riemann-surface definition requires; on a plane domain the meromorphic comparison correctly uses the function only off its pole set.

The identity charts on nonempty connected plane domains and the two sphere charts cover their spaces. The infinite-annulus radius is chosen finitely, so the atlas and connectedness premises remain valid.
The proof works in a connected chart neighbourhood of a nonconstant map, and the repaired atlas definition still supplies such local charts. Its use of the holomorphic-map interface is unchanged.

The index is taken from a nonconstant holomorphic map with chart expressions supplied by the unchanged local normal form. The corrected meromorphic plane-domain annotation does not alter this definition or its pole use.

Its source and target are connected Riemann surfaces by hypothesis, and local chart normal form plus properness gives finite fibres and local weighted counts. The repaired atlas and meromorphic conventions do not narrow these uses.

Both complex plane and punctured plane are connected plane domains, so their identity atlases satisfy the repaired definition. The exponential remains a holomorphic local biholomorphism with a noncompact fibre.

The changed Čech theorem clause concerns finite covers of the empty scheme; this counterexample uses a nonempty two-chart gluing and cites the separated comparison only for contrast, so its computation is unaffected.
Its explicit field-extension fibre condition now uses the corrected base-changed-fibre name and still defines smooth relative dimension zero; the changed terminology introduces no invalid proof use.
The Frobenius fibre is nonreduced and hence not geometrically regular; the revised étale definition still implies smoothness, so the counterexample and its use of F8 remain valid.
Its relation to ampleness uses the same fibre nonvanishing locus and later Serre criterion; the repaired proof that this locus is open changes neither global generation nor the cited implication.
The sheaf construction uses shifted modules with the same grading S(n)_d=S_(n+d); the corrected localization degree calculation in the supplier supports rather than changes the twist reference.
The definition O_X(n)=tilde(S(n)) uses the supplier sign convention unchanged; its local fraction degrees use deg(m)-deg(f)-n, matching the corrected localization calculation.
The unit section of O_X has nonzero fibre at every point under the repaired nonvanishing-locus definition. Its global generation and failure of relative very ampleness are unaffected.
The proof computes component dimensions m-r on every field-extended finite-type fibre chart; this is exactly the local-dimension convention now clarified by the supplier.
The polynomial chart has free parameter count n after every field extension, and n=0 is smooth of relative dimension zero. The revised fibre terminology changes no conclusion.
The already repaired Statement restricts local freeness to a neighbourhood of the smooth point. Its F6 uses finite-type fibre charts, where the corrected local-dimension formula applies.
The equivalence checks smooth relative dimension zero and the differential rank only on the smooth locus; both supplier interfaces retain precisely those hypotheses after repair.
The affine line is smooth of relative dimension one, with rank-one relative differentials; the corrected smooth-locus and fibre conventions still exclude étaleness.
The closed immersion has zero relative differentials but is not flat; the repaired étale definition still includes flatness through smoothness, so the witness remains valid.
The Čech comparison is applied to finite affine covers of actual inverse-image schemes; the supplier’s new empty-scheme clause also covers the explicitly treated empty base open.
The proof uses the unchanged affine-cover characterization of quasi-coherence. The supplier’s corrected commuting square only clarifies restriction maps and does not alter this pullback argument.

For finite-type field schemes the corrected supplier still identifies local dimension with the largest component dimension through the point; the local-ring plus residue-degree calculation uses exactly that case.
Its F5 and statement use the infimum-over-neighbourhoods definition, and its finite-type fibre argument uses the corrected component formula only under the permitted field hypothesis.

F2 had silently broadened associated-prime detection to possibly noncommutative Noetherian rings. It now retains the supplier’s commutative premise, satisfied by the local ring in the Statement; the determinantal proof is unchanged.
F3 now states the commutative premise of associated-prime detection. Its actual application is to S_g for a commutative affine scheme ring, so the nilpotent-minor argument remains licensed.

F6 formerly cited only the topological spectrum and module-sheaf definitions for D(f) being an affine scheme. It now cites the existing locally ringed-space localization isomorphism, licensing the common affine neighbourhood in step 3.1.
A section and its positive tensor power have the same nonzero fibre locus, so the repaired unit-germ proof of openness preserves the affine cover used in both directions of ampleness.
The criterion uses the same quasi-compact affine nonvanishing cover and affine restriction compatibility; the supplier repairs justify those interfaces without altering the coherent-twist argument.
Its use of an ample line bundle selects finitely many affine nonvanishing opens; the repaired supplier proves these are open and leaves their affine and positive-power hypotheses intact.
Relative ampleness tests the unchanged absolute ampleness condition on each inverse image of a base affine. The corrected proof of openness adds no new relative hypothesis.
The proof constructs global sections whose fibre nonvanishing opens are affine projective charts; the repaired intrinsic nonvanishing criterion identifies exactly those opens.
Its standard finite affine cover is nonempty for every projective n-space used, and the corrected Čech comparison still computes sheaf cohomology in every required degree.
The tensor proof applies the unchanged affine-cover equivalence to stalkwise tensor models; the repaired commutative square strengthens the restriction bookkeeping without invalidating a use.
The notation for twists under an ample sheaf uses the same intrinsic fibre nonvanishing convention and positive tensor powers; the repaired openness argument changes no twist definition.
Its finite affine nonvanishing cover and intersections use the same intrinsic fibre criterion, with affineness provided by the cited intersection lemma; the new unit-germ proof supports that use.
The proof applies ampleness only through affine nonvanishing sections and eventual generation; those hypotheses and resulting covers are unchanged by the supplier correction.
The coherent-pushforward argument uses an ample pullback of O(1) and finite affine Čech covers of separated schemes; both repaired suppliers preserve those actual interfaces.
The finite affine Čech complex remains a valid cohomology model for proper separated X, including the empty case with an empty or one-empty-open cover; no step depends on the old boundary wording.
F12 used g_T for pullbacks from both U and X, making the displayed base-change map ill-typed. It now names h:T→U and g_T:X_T→X, matching the supplier Statement while leaving the matrix proof intact.
The curvature contraction uses real multilinearity on real Lie algebras and complex multilinearity on complex Lie algebras, exactly as the corrected invariant-polynomial definition specifies.

The coefficientwise commutator cancellation invokes the infinitesimal invariance identity over the supplier’s stated scalar field; the corrected polarization convention leaves the graded-sign proof valid.
